Every component below is shown live, followed by the source that produced it.

## Key takeaways

Wrap a bulleted list in a `.takeaways` div. On a wide screen the script lifts it into the **right column** at the top of the page, which is where the box at the top right of this page came from. On a narrow screen it stays inline.

```markdown
::: {.takeaways}
- Short bullet one.
- Short bullet two.
:::
```

## Callouts

Quarto's built-in callouts are already themed.

::: {.callout-note}
## A note
Use for neutral background information.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## A warning
Use for mistakes that cost time.
:::

```markdown
::: {.callout-tip}
## Title
Body text.
:::
```

Types available: `note`, `tip`, `important`, `warning`, `caution`.

## Discussion prompt

Place a "Discuss first" box *before* the answer so learners commit to a guess.

```html
<div class="sm-discuss">
  <p class="sm-discuss-label"><i class="fa-solid fa-comments"></i>Discuss first</p>
  <p>What do you expect to happen, and why?</p>
</div>
```

Wrap raw HTML in a ```` ```{=html} ```` fence so Quarto passes it through untouched.

## Quizzes

Two types, graded in the browser with no server. **Multiple choice** matches the `value` of the chosen radio button to `data-answer`:

```{=html}
<div class="sm-quiz" data-quiz="mcq" data-answer="b">
  <p class="sm-quiz-q"><strong>Q1.</strong> How many options can be correct in a <code>mcq</code> quiz?</p>
  <div class="sm-quiz-options">
    <label><input type="radio" name="q-comp-1" value="a"> Any number</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="q-comp-1" value="b"> Exactly one</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="q-comp-1" value="c"> None</label>
  </div>
  <button class="sm-quiz-check">Check Answer</button>
  <div class="sm-quiz-feedback"></div>
</div>
```

**Fill in the blank** matches the typed text exactly (after trimming):

```{=html}
<div class="sm-quiz" data-quiz="fitb" data-answer="data-answer">
  <p class="sm-quiz-q"><strong>Q2.</strong> Which attribute holds the correct answer?</p>
  <div class="sm-quiz-fitb-row">
    <input type="text" class="sm-quiz-blank" placeholder="attribute" autocomplete="off" spellcheck="false">
  </div>
  <button class="sm-quiz-check">Check Answer</button>
  <div class="sm-quiz-feedback"></div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Unique radio names
Give each question its own radio `name` (for example `q-components-1`, `q-components-2`). Questions that share a name deselect each other.
:::

## Tabs and margin notes

Use Quarto tabsets to show alternatives side by side:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Markdown
```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}
## Tab one
Content
## Tab two
Content
:::
```
## Result
Exactly this: a row of tabs with one panel visible.
:::

Short asides, such as a glossary or a tip, go in the right column with `.column-margin`. Wherever you place them in the lesson, they are collected into the right-hand rail, between the resources and your notes.

::: {.column-margin}
**Margin note.** This sits in the right-hand column. Use it for definitions, tips and links that should not interrupt the main text.
:::

::: {.takeaways}
- `.takeaways` lifts into the right column.
- Quizzes are plain HTML with `data-quiz` and `data-answer`.
- Use `.column-margin` for asides and `.panel-tabset` for alternatives.
:::
